description:
Read one task of the workspace by its id: its title, description, status, priority, kind, parent task, assignee, due date and when it was done. It also returns `slot`: the calendar event booked for the job, with its own start and end, or null when the job has no slot yet or its slot is private to another member. Read the job's time from `slot` only; a task carries no time of its own, so a move of the event moves the slot. When the answer carries `slots_unavailable`, the calendar could not be read at all: the time is then unknown, and never say the job is unbooked. A plan (kind `plan`, such as an errand plan) also returns `steps`: its step tasks in step order, each with its id, title, status, kind and place in the plan. A browser task (kind `browser-task`) also returns `browser`: the browser action that runs it, its status, the browser it runs in, why it ended, its last step and the question it waits on (`open_ask_id`, to read with well_get_browser_action_ask), and `task_status`, where it stands now. A browser task that runs in a cloud browser on its own, one per shop, returns `web_task` instead: where that shop stands. Call it when the person's latest message only asks where a browser task stands ("so, the certificate?", "where is it at?", "alors, cette attestation ?", "où en est ma tâche ?"); well_list_tasks with `task_kind: "browser-task"` finds its id. When they ask where each shop stands, call it once for each open browser task. An ask that names a task the person saved starts that saved task instead. Never decide from the conversation that a browser task waits, runs or is done: only this result knows. On WhatsApp, Well sends `task_status` and `web_task` itself as a fixed line, so never write where the task stands. Only the task's own person (its assignee, or else its creator) who also started the browser action reads `browser` and `web_task`: for any other member they are null. A refund watch (kind `claim` after a return or a cancellation) also returns `refund_watch`: the merchant and its e-mail addresses in Well (`merchant_emails`, the only ones a chase may go to), the expected refund and day, its `state` (`watching`, `overdue`: the day passed with no credit and Well has not chased yet, `chased`, `refund_seen`: the credit is in the bank feed, `closed`), when Well chased the merchant and noted the refund mail, the matched credit, and `bank_read` (false when the bank feed could not be read in full). Only the person of the browser task that sent the return reads `refund_watch`. A hold Well placed on a website with no payment (kind `site-hold`) also returns `site_hold`: the site, what is held, its reference and amount, when it expires, its `state` (`held`, `reminded`, `resuming`: a browser task works on it, `expired`, or how it ended), what a confirm does (`confirm_by`) and what a release does (`release_by`); only its own person reads it, and well_update_site_hold confirms or lets it go. It changes nothing. A guest reads only the tasks assigned to them.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

task_id.description: The task, from well_list_tasks or an earlier result.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_get_task

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

title: Get task
